For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic portrait, the woman shown in <Picture 1> raises her hand toward her wavy blonde hair, gently touching a strand beside her shoulder while maintaining direct eye contact with the camera. Her lips part and the woman with a clear, melodic voice (S1) says: <d>[English] Do you like my hair?</d> Her jaw and lips move clearly through every word. She closes her lips into a soft smile, lowers her hand, and the camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed as she settles into a confident final pose, preserving her facial identity, red satin dress, gold jewelry, and warm studio lighting throughout.

overall_soundscape: Quiet indoor room tone continues throughout with faint fabric rustle and soft breathing.

non_diegetic_music: Warm, sparse electric piano chords at a slow tempo with a gentle atmospheric bed, gradually fading out.

nodes.title: Sampler settings (tested)
widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

SAMPLER SETTINGS FOR THE SPEED LORA

Tested on this exact workflow: 54 renders. Six sampler and scheduler pairings, each rendered from 3 different starting pictures (a portrait in a red dress, a geisha with dense pattern, and a building with no face in it) and 3 different seeds.

First frame mode is judged on one thing: does the first frame of the video still look like the picture you put in? That is measured as the average difference between the two. Under about 5 you cannot tell them apart. Over about 20 it is a different picture, not a worse one.

THE SHORT VERSION

Any of the five below is fine. Never use ddim_uniform. That is the real finding: among the sensible pairings the differences are tiny and you would not spot them side by side, while ddim_uniform does not just look worse, it throws your picture away completely.

PICK ONE FROM THE DROPDOWN

CombinationScoreDifferenceNotes
euler + beta8.53.74The default here. Beat each of the others in 5 of 8 comparisons, which is a real but small edge.
euler + simple8.03.87Just as good in practice. This is the one text to video prefers, so use it if you want both workflows on the same setting.
euler + sgm_uniform8.03.87Identical in practice to simple.
res_multistep + simple8.04.16Fine. What most of your older H3 workflows already use.
dpmpp_sde_gpu + sgm_uniform6.55.56Still good, slightly behind the rest, and slower to render.


DO NOT USE ddim_uniform

It scored 1 out of 10 and failed on every single one of its nine renders. It does not degrade the picture, it replaces it: the red dress portrait turned into a wall of scattered photographs of a different woman. Every other pairing kept the dress, the face and the pose.

This is worth knowing because a widely shared sampler benchmark recommends ddim_uniform pairings. It is measuring picture quality and motion, and never asks whether you got the picture you asked for.


SOME PICTURES ARE HARDER THAN OTHERS

The building with no face in it was the hardest: on one of the three seeds every single pairing failed to hold it, including the good ones. Faces and people were held reliably by all five. So if a start picture will not hold, try another seed before you blame the sampler.



STEPS: USE 8, NOT 4

The LoRA is called a 4 step LoRA and 4 steps is enough for the picture. It is not enough for the sound. Found by blind listening: four clips, same seed, only the step count different, names shuffled and the volume matched so loudness could not give it away. Ranked best to worst, twice, with different seeds:

12 > 8 > 6 > 4 both times. The odds of that happening twice by chance are about 1 in 576.

StepsSoundPictureTime
4Worst, both rounds3.3028sWhat the LoRA is named after
6Third3.2934s
8Second3.3038sUse this. Same picture as 4, better sound, 10 seconds more.
12Best4.2952sSounds best but the picture drifts from your input, on every seed tested

The picture column is how closely the first frame still matches the starting image, lower is better. Notice it is flat from 4 to 8 and then gets worse at 12: the LoRA was distilled for a small number of steps, and 12 pushes it outside what it was trained for.

Measuring tools could NOT find this. Harshness, noisiness and echo were all measured across 54 clips and found nothing, and on echo they pointed the wrong way. Only listening found it.

THE OTHER SETTING THAT MATTERS

The Shift 6 node feeding the sampler. This LoRA was trained for shift 6, while the model on its own defaults to 12. Leave it at 6.


IF YOU WANT THE SAME VIDEO AGAIN

Set control after generate under the seed to fixed. On randomize the seed changes after every run, so dragging a video back in and pressing Run gives you a different clip.
